Where'd you go?
Kia ora. Rangitane Tangata Rau, Rangitane Nui, Rangitane
Whitu ki te rangi ko Rangitane ki te whenua. Tena tatou katoa.
E hoa tatou tenni mate. O tera i tenei kaupapa a tatou.
Kia ora, members. My name is Corey Hebbert.
I'm the General Manager for Rangitane Owairu, joined by Dr Peter Meihana,
who is both a trustee of Rangitane Owairu and the Te Hiri Anuku Trust.
Mm-hmm.
Before we begin, just want to acknowledge the significant weather events affecting
Te Tauihu in the past 24 hours, and particularly our whanaungia in Kaikōura to the
south.
There's been significant flooding, road closures, and disruptions, so our thoughts
with everyone in the region.
Kia ora.
I also want to acknowledge Matawaroari Stafford and his whānau.
The fact that this bill is before you today reflects decades of effort by many
people, with Matawaroari central to ensuring that this matter
continues to progress towards its final resolution.
Rangitane Owairu supports the Te Hiri Anuku Nelson Tents Bill.
While Rangitane is not a direct beneficiary under the legislation or the
resolution agreement, many of our whānau descend from tūpuna connected to the
Nelson Tents lands and the wider history behind this grievance.
The Nelson Tents issue has been examined extensively through litigation, historical
research, Crown engagement, and negotiation.
The history is well known, the findings are well documented, and the Crown has
acknowledged that obligations associated with the Tents reserves were not honored
as originally intended.
This committee is not being asked to determine whether a grievance exists.
The question that is before you is whether effect should now be given to the
resolution agreement reached between Te Hiri Anuku Trust and the Crown through this
bill.
We believe it should.
This resolution is significant not only because it resolves matters arising from
the Nelson Tents litigation, but because it enables the Crown to complete
commitments that have already been made, including aspects of Treaty settlement
redress that have remained unresolved as a consequence of that litigation.
Auckland Point School in Nelson provides a useful example.
The school forms part of the Rangitane Owairu Treaty settlement.
Rangitane exercised its right to purchase the property in March 2015 and
has since been the beneficial owner.
However, legal title could not transfer because the property remained subject to a
caveat associated with the Nelson Tents litigation and lands within the Spain Award
area.
As a result, Treaty settlement redress that had already been agreed could not be
fully implemented by the Crown.
Following the resolution agreement reached in December last year, the Crown
confirmed that the redress can proceed as originally intended.
The lifting of the caveat has enabled the transfer process to move forward and
removed uncertainty that has existed since the time of our settlement.
Auckland Point School is just one example, but it demonstrates that the
consequences of the Nelson Tents litigation extended beyond the
lands directly affected by the proceedings.
This bill does more than transfer land and assets to Te Hiri Anuku Trust.
It implements the resolution agreement. It gives effect to court findings.
It provides certainty regarding property and governance arrangements within Te
Tauihu, and it enables longstanding Treaty settlement commitments to also
finally be completed. The resolution agreement signed on the
17th of December 2025 was the product of extensive
negotiation between Te Hiri Anuku and the Crown.
Parliament now has the opportunity to give effect to that agreement.
I also wish to briefly address the inclusion of the Kura Haupo tūpuna, as this has
been raised by some submitters.
Rangitane's support for this bill is consistent with the findings of the Waitangi
Tribunal and the Crown's own acknowledgments.
The Tribunal found that Rangitane tūpuna and Kura Haupo tūpuna
should have been beneficiaries of the Nelson Tents reserve, while the Crown
has acknowledged that Rangitane did not receive a share of those reserves.
This matter forms part of the historical record and provides important
context for the inclusion of those Kura Haupo tūpuna.
I also note public concerns regarding future access arrangements.
Those concerns, we believe, should be viewed in context.
This legislation relates to land that the courts found was held by the
Crown on trust for descendants of the customary owners.
Te Hiri Anuku Trust has committed to maintaining existing arrangements for at least
25 years and has stated that future arrangements will be guided by
principles of partnership, kaitiakitanga, and stewardship.
In our view, that should provide confidence to the committee and to the public that
this bill is about implementing a negotiated resolution, not
about restricting public access.
In summary, the Nelson Tents grievance is longstanding and is well
documented, and it has already been extensively
examined. This bill gives effect to the resolution agreement
reached between Te Hiri Anuku Trust and the Crown.
Auckland Point School demonstrates how the litigation affected wider Crown Treaty
settlement commitments, including our own Treaty settlement redress.
This bill enables longstanding settlement commitments to be completed and provides
certainty for the future.
Parliament now has the opportunity to implement the agreed resolution through this
legislation. For those reasons, Rangitane Owairu
supports the bill and respectfully encourages the committee to
recommend that it proceed.
In closing, I want to place on record Rangitane's acknowledgments to Dr Peter
Meihana and Nicole Akuhaza for their work on behalf of the three Kura Haupo
iwi and our people, the trustees of Te Hiri Anuku Trust,
the many whānau who have supported this kaupapa over many years, and former
Attorney General Honorable Judith Collins and the Crown officials involved in
reaching the resolution agreement.
Finally, I again want to acknowledge Matawaroari Stafford and his whānau, whose
longstanding commitment, and indeed sacrifice, has been instrumental to
bringing the matter to this point.
Mr Chair, we're happy to take any questions with the time remaining.
Thank you. A very clear submission.
We've got Dan Rosewarne.
Yeah. Hey, thanks, Corey, for that detailed submission.
You spoke about the history, the shared history of Te Tauihu
iwi within your submission, and I was just wondering what
opportunities do you see this bill creating for future
collaboration between the descendants of the customary owners
and the wider iwi within the region?
Sure. So to tell you who has a rich tapestry of whakapapa, many
of us whakapapa are across the multiple iwi within the region.
I myself, across the nine iwi of Te Waipounamu, whakapapa to nine.
Pete, I think you whakapapa to most.
So already there's existing collaborations through existing treaty settlement
arrangements and the like, where we do work collaboratively and constructively
together. The eight iwi collaborate in a multi-vehicle
trust and other mechanisms. So I see this very much as continuing
the work that has gone on before, but importantly, enabling completion of those
outstanding matters in respect of the Nelson tents, which of course have been
longstanding matters unresolved outside of treaty settlement processes.
But certainly provides a really strong footing that gives effect to some of those
aspirations that I know our people would have had at the time of the tents
being formed.
Thanks, Corey.
Thanks, Dan. Steve Abel.
Oh, sorry, just found my audio button.
Thank you very much for that substantive and really clear submission.
Can you give us a bit more detail on the specific Auckland School issue, and
how the passage of this bill
resolves that?
Sure. So Auckland Point School was a deferred settlement property within the
Rangitane settlement. We passed our settlement in August 2014,
and then had the option to exercise a right of first refusal to purchase land at
Auckland Point School. Due to the Stafford litigation, there was a
caveat placed on the school by Wakatu Incorporation at the time, as it was
advancing proceedings on behalf of the customary owners.
As a result of the resolution agreement having been reached, and as a result of
this legislation now moving through its passage, that's given the ability
for that caveat to be lifted and for the Crown to take steps to transfer legal
title of that property through to Rangitane.
It has been prevented from doing that to date, which means that that treaty
settlement commitment has been unable to be put into place.
And so this enables, obviously, the intent of our treaty settlement
commitments and the Crown to fulfill its obligations to transfer legal
title consistent with the original
intent.
Okay, brilliant. Thank you.
Thank you both for your submission.
Very clear and, yeah, great to have something
so supportive as well. Appreciate your time today.

the situation is
we've been here for 60-odd years.

A very large area, and we administer it and look

people operating

A significant amount of money for people that, and an

be recompensed for the loss,
so that we can continue the work that we are set up to do.
That's your 10 minutes.

That's your 10 minutes.

Righto.

just in a very quick essence of it,
Clause 109 of the bill

Carina may want to make just a couple of comments first.

Nelson Tenants Bill. So the matters raised in the submission

There's likely to be an income stream required.
We don't know yet whether they will actually have to be relocated from this land or
